neighbourhoods.name: Solihull town centre
neighbourhoods.housing: Flats near Touchwood and the station, with Edwardian and inter-war houses on the surrounding roads.

neighbourhoods.name: Shirley
neighbourhoods.housing: Inter-war and post-war semis and terraces along the Stratford Road, with newer estates to the south.

neighbourhoods.name: Olton
neighbourhoods.housing: Inter-war semi-detached and detached houses around Olton station and the reservoir.

neighbourhoods.name: Knowle and Dorridge
neighbourhoods.housing: Large detached and semi-detached houses, many from the inter-war and post-war years, around village centres.

neighbourhoods.name: Balsall Common
neighbourhoods.housing: Post-war and newer detached and semi-detached houses in a commuter village.

neighbourhoods.name: Chelmsley Wood
neighbourhoods.housing: A large 1960s and 70s estate of council-built houses, maisonettes and tower blocks, now with many privately let ex-council homes.

neighbourhoods.name: Kingshurst and Smith's Wood
neighbourhoods.housing: Post-war estates of terraced houses and low-rise flats north of Chelmsley Wood.

neighbourhoods.name: Castle Bromwich
neighbourhoods.housing: Inter-war and post-war semi-detached family houses on the edge of Birmingham.

neighbourhoods.name: Elmdon and Marston Green
neighbourhoods.housing: Inter-war and post-war semis close to Birmingham Airport and the NEC.

housing: Solihull is one of the most owner-occupied boroughs in the West Midlands. The south, around Solihull town, Knowle, Dorridge and Balsall Common, is mostly inter-war and post-war semi-detached and detached family housing, much of it in the Green Belt. The north, around Chelmsley Wood, Kingshurst and Smith's Wood, was built as overspill housing for Birmingham in the 1960s and 70s and has more social and ex-council homes now let privately. Lets near the airport, the NEC and Jaguar Land Rover draw workers and commuters.
checkinTips: Ex-council houses and maisonettes in Chelmsley Wood and Kingshurst: record the boiler, fencing, communal stairs, bin stores and door entry system.
Larger family homes in Knowle, Dorridge and Shirley: photograph gardens, hedges, garages, driveways and conservatories, which tenants are often expected to keep up.
Flats in Solihull town centre: note fob, key and parking permit counts and the post box and bin store arrangements.
Homes near Birmingham Airport in Elmdon and Marston Green: record the windows and any secondary glazing or acoustic insulation.
Tower blocks in the north of the borough: photograph fire doors, smoke alarms and any building safety notices in the communal areas.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact Solihull Council's private sector housing team, which can inspect homes and take action against landlords.
